claims.claim: The determinant of the unit projection basis is sqrt(3)/2.
claims.falsifier: Direct determinant differs beyond floating tolerance.
H^T H differs from the declared metric.

claims.claim: The six axial neighbor directions project to unit distance.
claims.falsifier: Any declared neighbor has projected distance different from one.

claims.claim: Matrices A and B use the hexagonal basis as a common projection page.
claims.falsifier: The implementation uses a different index order or basis without versioning.

claims.claim: The A×B geometric relation tensor has 840 records and two spatial components.
A projected cone necessarily produces a physical Venturi mechanism.
claims.falsifier: No fluid variables, governing equations, boundary conditions or measurements are supplied.

claims.claim: A toroidal embedding necessarily represents a physical vortex or cosmological structure.
claims.falsifier: No physical field, units, data or causal model are supplied.

claims.claim: A ring torus is radially bounded from the origin by R-r and R+r.
claims.falsifier: The norm of the standard torus embedding falls outside the declared interval.

claims.claim: The meridian section is the circle (rho-R)^2+z^2=r^2 with upper and lower semicircular branches.
claims.falsifier: Substitution of the standard embedding does not satisfy the circle equation.

claims.claim: The largest equilateral triangle inscribed in the meridian circle has side sqrt(3)*r.
claims.falsifier: Three points separated by 120 degrees do not have equal chord length sqrt(3)*r.

claims.claim: All rotations of a centered square share an inner disk of radius s/2 and sweep an outer disk of radius s/sqrt(2).
claims.falsifier: The square inradius or circumradius differs from the declared values.

claims.claim: Line-meridian intersections reduce to a quadratic equation classified by the discriminant.
claims.falsifier: Substitution of z=m*rho+b does not produce the declared coefficients.

claims.claim: Tangents constrained to 30 degrees use slopes plus or minus 1/sqrt(3) and satisfy Delta=0.
claims.falsifier: The generated lines are not tangent or do not have the declared slopes.

claims.claim: A frequency-f subdivided icosahedral sphere has V=10f^2+2, E=30f^2 and F=20f^2.
claims.falsifier: The counts fail V-E+F=2 or disagree with subdivision combinatorics.

claims.claim: For linear flow on T^2, the u-section return map is P(v)=v+2*pi*(omega_v/omega_u) mod 2*pi.
claims.falsifier: Direct integration of constant angular velocities yields a different return.

claims.claim: The linear return map proves recurrence or stability for a measured physical vortex.
claims.falsifier: No physical equations, parameters, observations or nonlinear stability analysis are supplied.

guards: Exact geometry may be PASS while physical claims remain TOKEN_VAZIO.
Similarity of sqrt(3) factors does not establish causal identity.
Toro geometry is not equivalent to vortex dynamics.
Cone geometry is not equivalent to the Venturi effect.
R-r and R+r are Euclidean radial bounds, not torus geodesic distances.
The upper and lower meridian branches are semicircles, not parabolas.
Bhaskara solves the line-circle intersection; it does not define the geometry alone.
Thirty degrees is an imposed and tested tangent condition.
The implemented Poincare map is for linear T^2 flow, not the Poincare conjecture.
An icosphere is a triangular approximation of a sphere after radial projection.
RafPolimata records semantics and evidence; ChipQuantum owns runtime implementation.
